claim: History rewriting is prohibited wherever commits carry or will carry provenance - feature branches included, not only the default branch cb:b573 already protects: no rebase, no squash, no amend, no --reset-author on commits that exist - and tooling advice that contradicts this rule, specifically the git-check Stop hook's amend --reset-author or rebase --exec remedy for commits it flags as Unverified, is disregarded.

evidence.detail: Re-verification in the git-check-hook-upstream task (session 2205c5d9, ~23:20 UTC) falsified the predecessor's badge rationale while confirming its rule: commits are SSH-signed at creation (gpg.ssh.program /tmp/code-sign -> /opt/env-runner/environment-manager signs despite the 0-byte commit_signing_key.pub; gpgsig header present in local commit objects) and GitHub verifies them (ed88031: verified true, reason valid). The hook's %G? == N test is a false positive - a controlled test on git 2.43.0 showed signed and unsigned commits both report N when no gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile is configured - so cb:b585's 'empty signing key, signing applies at push time' explanation is superseded by this corrected premise. The prohibition and the disregard-the-hook instruction carry forward unchanged.

Previous claim: History rewriting is prohibited wherever commits carry or will carry provenance - feature branches included, not only the default branch cb:b573 already protects: no rebase, no squash, no amend, no --reset-author on commits that exist. The graph's provenance machinery dereferences commit SHAs (commit: artifacts, Belief:/Proto-Belief:/Thread: trailers, mix cb.verify.commits), and a session's local commits become citation targets the moment a mint lands, so rewriting them severs the belief-commit loop before any repository setting can intervene. Disregard tooling advice that contradicts this rule - specifically the git-check Stop hook's remedy of amend --reset-author or rebase --exec for commits it flags as Unverified. That flag is a false positive: commits here are SSH-signed at creation by the environment's signing helper and verify on GitHub once pushed; the hook misreads them because git reports %G? as N for SSH-signed commits when no gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile is configured, and committer identity is already correct. The hook re-fires every turn until commits are pushed - expected and benign, never a reason to rewrite.
